clue.text: Unionist hampered by broken leg? This should fix it

indicators.note: a person hampered by something is hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside the other
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken leg that has slowed down a Unionist politician needs mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampered by' puts U inside GLE, the anagram of LEG signalled by 'broken'. The question mark warns the definition is a whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive is the thing you use to mend something broken.

clue.text: Complained of being burgled, unfortunately, with money taken

indicators.note: money taken in is held inside, so one piece goes into the other
things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters of burgled are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moaned after a break-in in which cash was stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' makes GRUBLED from BURGLED, and 'taken' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble is to moan or complain.

clue.text: Not yet solid as peacekeeping group?

parts.note: the UN (United Nations) sends peacekeeping forces
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A question about whether something not yet solid is a peacekeeping body.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a 'UN set', a group of peacekeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly or concrete that has not hardened is still fluid.

clue.text: River Niagara meanders in the fields

indicators.note: a meandering river wanders about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Niagara River winds its way through farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meanders' shuffles R and NIAGARA together. The definition is an adjectival phrase: farming takes place in the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to land and farming, the work done out on cultivated ground.

clue.text: Book is following things which control heredity

indicators.note: IS comes after the other piece, following it in the answer

parts.note: genes are the units that pass on inherited traits

explanation.surface: A book about genetics.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Old Testament is named for the creation it recounts.

clue.text: Old man's conservative study of Hittites?

parts.note: ancient means very old
his means belonging to a man
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An elderly man's conservative-minded research into the Hittites.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hittites were an ancient people, so studying them is an example of the subject, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship on the Hittites belongs to the discipline covering the civilisations of antiquity.

clue.text: Perhaps the character of Jeremy is potentially attractive

parts.note: Jeremy Irons is the English actor
tone can mean character or quality

explanation.surface: A remark that the actor Jeremy's personality might be appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Jeremy as one example of the surname IRONS; 'the character of Jeremy' gives Irons' TONE. The definition plays on magnetic attraction, since this rock is an iron ore.
explanation.definitionFit: This iron-bearing rock can be drawn to a magnet, so it is potentially attractive in the magnetic sense.

clue.text: Unless I leave the moral standard will be overturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sin is to depart from what is morally right

explanation.surface: Someone warns that unless they quit, morality will be overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be overturned' reverses I SIN to give the Latin word, familiar from the decree nisi in divorce law.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for 'if not' is kept in English legal language, as in decree nisi.

clue.text: Cast covering wound of Trojan prince?

parts.note: a plaster is a dressing stuck over a cut
Paris was the prince of Troy who abducted Helen

explanation.surface: A dressing over an injury suffered by a prince of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a verb but is the noun: a rigid mould set round a broken limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A white gypsum powder that sets hard when wet is used to make casts for broken bones.

clue.text: Cake: see about eating 250?

indicators.note: a word eating another takes it inside itself
about here signals that the word see is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
CCL is 250 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A question whether a cake contains 250 calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the word round before 'eating' wraps it round the Roman numeral. ECCLES is a town near Manchester that gives its name to a currant-filled pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A round flaky pastry filled with currants is named after a Lancashire town.

clue.text: Conclusion: fuse's faulty? Not a bit concerned

indicators.note: something faulty is not working properly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of fuse's, read without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An electrician concludes that the fuse is broken but is not bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' shuffles the fifteen letters of CONCLUSION and FUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at ease is free of embarrassment or awkward self-awareness.

clue.text: They improve ablutions of West of England sailors?

parts.note: Bath is a city in the west of England
salts are old sailors

explanation.surface: A question whether West Country seamen make washing better.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a spa city in Somerset, in the west of England. 'old salt' is a familiar term for a seasoned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystals dissolved in the tub make bathing more pleasant.

clue.text: Stop to remove cape and relax

indicators.note: the cape is taken away from the word for stop

parts.note: to cease is to stop
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: An instruction to take off a cloak and unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment to take off, but it is C, the map abbreviation for a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to slacken or relax.

clue.text: Ruler wants me to return papers

indicators.note: returning means the word me is read backwards

parts.note: the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: A monarch demands the newspapers be brought back to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sovereign, or the wife of an emperor, rules an empire.

clue.text: Outlook for song is bad

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: something bad is spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy forecast for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' signals the anagram of the middle stretch only; 'for' gives the Latin-derived word meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast of how things, especially an illness, are likely to turn out.

clue.text: Playing in Test, so struggles

indicators.note: playing about with letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match being contested with difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' shuffles TEST and SO. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Set-tos are fights or arguments, brief struggles.

clue.text: Made niche seceders exploited

indicators.note: exploited here means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breakaway members were used and created a niche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploited' rearranges SECEDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that has been set back has had an alcove made in it.

clue.text: Poor adaptation by American allowing penetration of water

indicators.note: an adaptation changes the form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weak remake of a film by an American studio about water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation' rearranges POOR into PORO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of tiny holes lets liquid soak through.

clue.text: Seen, improbably, to comprehend state of some triangles

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include, so one piece holds the other
improbably suggests things are not as expected, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CAL is the abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Something seen unexpectedly helps someone understand geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improbably' signals the anagram and 'to comprehend' the container; 'state' is a US state abbreviation, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle with all three sides unequal is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Mandarin inches off towards east

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of inches are rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A mandarin orange rolling a few inches eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges INCHES into CHINES. 'Mandarin' is not the fruit but the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main language of China, so it is an example of the national tongue.

clue.text: Pursued, we hear, but virtuous

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is said out loud and sounds like another

parts.note: chased means pursued

explanation.surface: Someone was pursued but remained pure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns CHASED into a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaste person is pure and morally good.

clue.text: Break kitchen items over here

indicators.note: over here says the word for the kitchen items is turned round

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels used in a kitchen

explanation.surface: Crockery is being smashed in this kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over here' reverses PANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly with a crack.

clue.text: Showing versatility, a page brings lawyer in a supply of food

indicators.note: the lawyer goes inside the first two pieces

parts.note: DA is an American district attorney
a table is food provided, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A young servant brings a lawyer into a buffet, proving flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts DA inside A and P. DA, District Attorney, is an American lawyer; a 'table' is the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flexible can adjust to new roles and conditions.

clue.text: Turbot? Chef's bound to make a mess of things

indicators.note: bound means the letters are tied up inside the words

explanation.surface: A cook with a turbot is certain to ruin the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' signals the answer is held in TurBOT CHef's.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch is to do a job clumsily.

clue.text: Seaweed turning up in river again

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seaweed floating back to the surface in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This jelly comes from red algae, a kind of marine plant.

clue.text: Interrogates -it's bad — giving rise to complaint

indicators.note: bad means wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Questioning someone harshly brings on illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges INTERROGATES and ITS. 'complaint' means an illness here, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflammation of the stomach and gut is an ailment.

clue.text: Opposed relative mostly 9 wearing scarlet

indicators.note: something wearing a colour has it on the outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sister is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member dressed in scarlet stood against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter and 'wearing' puts the relative inside the colour. The '9' gives nothing to the wordplay and looks like a misprint for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resisted something is to have fought against it.

clue.text: Unhappy about Henry's fish

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: sad means unhappy
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A sad man named Henry and his fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H inside SAD. The henry is the physics unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: A shad is a herring-like fish.
